projection: equirectangular, north up, east to the right; ROTATED 180 deg about the sub-planet axis (south up: the client mesh +Y is the IAU south pole of this retrograde moon); lon 0 at the centre

align.note: no previous site map: USGS orientation (lon 0 at the centre)

normal: tangent space x=east y=north z=up, IMAGE-DERIVED (no global DEM): band-pass luminance (6 px at 8k) as height, bright = high, RMS slope 5 deg where the mosaic is sharp (x Q), x 0.7 in filled areas
colour: the mosaic's own colour, saturation x0.15; harsh terminator lighting soft-clamped to the local median; low-resolution areas de-ringed; gaps filled (wavy ramp <= 128 px, ring inpaint); polar caps de-rippled in an azimuthal grid; multiplicative sphere-noise grain (0.6 x local detail); luminance mean 124 (from the measured geometric albedo) (tone power 1.000); no blue cast; unseen areas: smooth continuation of the data + band-pass detail of the body's own imaged terrain seen through rotations of the sphere (sources |lat| <= 60; a plausible stand-in, not observed); low-resolution areas carry band-pass detail of Triton's own sharp terrain through 5 sphere rotations, weight (1-Q)
source: USGS Astrogeology: Triton Voyager 2 Global Color Mosaic 600 m
